I would record Ryan’s absence as **UA**, but urgently flag the consequences for human review before payroll runs.

Under the codes given, Ryan was not ill, his sister was not a member of his household, and the absence was not booked in advance. So SC and DEP do not fit, even though he had a compelling reason to be absent. Leaving SC in place would knowingly give payroll an incorrect reason.

I would add a factual note that Ryan called at 05:40, before his shift, and was helping his sister during unexpected labour. The note should make clear that UA does **not** mean he failed to call or had no reason for being absent.

Before 12:00, I would email payroll, the appropriate manager and HR urgently, explaining that this would be Ryan’s second UA and would automatically trigger a termination letter. I would ask whether someone with authority can review the case or hold the letter. I would not assume that email will be read in time or that I can override the probation rule: on the facts given, the letter will be sent if no authorised intervention occurs.
